name: The Axtell household — a name from the post office's letter lists
head: axtell_almond

arrival.note: A BOUND FROM THE RETURN, NOT AN ARRIVAL. The office's list of letters uncalled-for is a RETURN — its statement of what was still unclaimed on ONE day — and the paper reprinted one return over as many consecutive issues as it took, so the bound is dated by the return of 1 January 1834 and not by the issue it was read in (T-0425). The earliest issue this project reads the name in is 1834-03-04, 62 days later; that gap is an accident of which impression an extraction pass reached, and it is not evidence. Somebody was writing to this name at Chicago by 1834-01-01 and at no stated time before it; nothing says when they came. The date lines the printings set, and how they were weighed, stand beside this rule in tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py.

lives_at.note: Not attested: a letter list gives a name and no address.

works_at.note: Not attested. No trade is recorded, so there is no premises to seek.

present_on_scene_date.note: THE CORPUS STOPS BEFORE THE SCENE DATE. Nothing after 1834-03-04 follows this person to 1 July 1835 or says they left. `uncertain` rather than dropped — the distinction index.json draws for Jeremiah Porter, and a finding, not a gap.

occupation.note: No source records an occupation for this person. A list of uncalled-for letters prints a name and no trade, and this pass will not read one in.

persons.note: KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print 'Almond Axtell 2' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 4 March 1834 — dated 1834-03-04. READ AT THE PAGE IMAGE, OFF THE PRINTED LINE, AND MINTED ONLY NOW. This person's evidence is line 5 of the return as it stands in the ninth and last of the nine impressions of this return, set `Almond Axtell 2` and read at the scan by T-0424 (data/research/newspapers/letter_list_1834_01_01_printed.json). NO TRANSCRIPTION OF ANY IMPRESSION CARRIES IT: the crops this project extracted from have an advertisement interleaved through the list, and it swallowed this line along with 53 others — which is the whole reason the name reached no card for a year of this corpus's work, and is not a judgement anybody made about it (T-1010 measured the gap, T-1011 closed it). The line ends on `2`, which on this list is the COUNT OF LETTERS WAITING and not a middle initial — the roster records that notation itself — so the count is carried beside the name and the name is the line without it. The reading is the scan's, so it is the strongest kind this cohort holds; what it says is still only that a letter was waiting. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1).

research_note: MINTED FROM THE LETTER LISTS (T-0378, T-0379). THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here argues for a household, and this one argues for a PERSON. `data/residents/` cannot carry a person outside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing — one member, no dwelling, no division, no trade, no family, no arrival beyond the paper's bound. tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py derives the set and prints every refusal, `--gate` proves no record here gained a roof, a trade or a second member, and docs/LIBERTIES.md L214 carries the change of scale.
